clue.text: Advantage anticipated by Russian singer

indicators.note: one piece being anticipated by another means the second comes first

parts.note: red is the old shorthand for a Soviet Russian, from the Red Army
a start is a head start, an advantage given before a race

explanation.surface: A Russian vocalist has a head start over rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'singer' is a songbird, not a vocalist: the redstart is a small European bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a songbird, and crosswords often call any bird a singer.

clue.text: Subpoena'd again, gave a detailed account

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to be cited is to be summoned to court

explanation.surface: A witness called back to court told the whole story.
explanation.walkthrough: To recite is to list or relate in detail, as well as to say a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite facts is to enumerate them one by one, narrating them fully.

clue.text: Shingle headland needs guns deployed

indicators.note: guns deployed are spread out and rearranged, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A pebbly point on the coast requires artillery set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges NEEDS and GUNS. Dungeness is a vast shingle promontory on the Kent coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungeness is a cape in Kent formed of shingle, home to a nuclear power station.

clue.text: Pushes corrosive agent, replacing one in this?

indicators.note: the corrosive agent takes the place of the one in this word

parts.note: taken as written
one is I in Roman numerals
rust eats into iron, corroding it

explanation.surface: A chemist forces an acid in to stand in for a component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps the I of THIS for RUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrusts are shoves or forceful drives forward.

clue.text: Entries for the singles, maybe

explanation.surface: Listings for unattached people.
explanation.walkthrough: Singles here are short discs of pop music, not unmarried people.
explanation.definitionFit: Records are written entries in a log, and a single is a short vinyl disc of a song.

clue.text: Nothing jolly in profitable layout

indicators.note: the nothing and jolly pieces are placed within the profitable word

parts.note: a fat contract or fee is a lucrative one
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A dull spreadsheet design makes money but has no fun in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective but is the slang term for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: The format of a page or book is its arrangement and design.

clue.text: Strand clubman's *warning on horseplay

parts.note: golfers shout fore to warn others of a ball in flight

indicators.note: play means the letters are given free movement and rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer shouts a caution about some horsing around on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strand' is the seashore, not a thread; the clubman is a golfer, not a club member. 'play' rearranges HORSE into SHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is the edge of the sea, the beach between tides.

clue.text: Anger about a member's violent behaviour

indicators.note: about means the anger word goes round the a and member pieces

parts.note: rage is fury, extreme anger
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at an MP's thuggish conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AMP after the R of RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of wild, destructive conduct.

clue.text: Rural setting for vulgar type in song

indicators.note: the vulgar type is placed within the song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
a cad is an ungentlemanly, ill-bred man

explanation.surface: A country scene suits a coarse man in a ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the idealised pastoral land of Greek legend, a paradise of shepherds.

clue.text: He may build a sort of bridge with gold

parts.note: contract bridge is the standard form of the card game
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A builder might construct a bridge using gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge is the card game, not a structure, which the builder in the surface invites you to picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A contractor is a firm or person hired to carry out building work.

clue.text: Polly Peachum's lover's protection against downfall

explanation.surface: A heroine's sweetheart guards her from ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly Peachum is the heroine of The Beggar's Opera and The Threepenny Opera; her lover Macheath is Mack the Knife. The 'downfall' is rain, not ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Macheath is called Mack the Knife in Brecht's song, and a mack is a raincoat that keeps off a shower.

clue.text: Novel source of wealth for Trelawney

explanation.surface: A new way for a squire to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: Squire Trelawney funds the voyage in Stevenson's novel, and the place gives him a fortune in buried gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's book is the famous pirate adventure, and the place of the title holds Captain Flint's hoard.

clue.text: Lines up shifts, perhaps

explanation.surface: A foreman organises the rota for the work shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers dress their ranks when they line up straight; a shift is a simple style of frock.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a line of troops is to straighten it, and a shift is a loose frock, one kind of garment for women.

clue.text: Heart-broken protégé discloses eventual direction of Longfellow's arrow

indicators.note: a broken heart is shattered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ward is someone under a guardian's protection

explanation.surface: A lovesick young charge reveals where a poet's dart ended up.
explanation.walkthrough: Longfellow's poem The Arrow and the Song says the arrow 'fell to earth, I knew not where'. 'broken' rearranges HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: The arrow came down, so it went groundward in the end.

clue.text: Began, so clumsily, to make a food container

indicators.note: something done clumsily is botched, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone awkwardly starts to make a lunchbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsily' rearranges BEGAN and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is a feed bag hung over a horse's head, holding its oats.

clue.text: Form of extortion shunned by striking postmen

explanation.surface: Strikers in the post office refuse to touch a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: Strikers 'black' goods they refuse to handle, so mail they boycott is black mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackmail is extortion by threat of exposure, and blacked post is what union members decline to deliver.

clue.text: A way to divide unspoiled grassland

indicators.note: the A and the way piece split the unspoiled word into two parts

parts.note: unspoiled means untainted, pure
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A path cuts across untouched meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to divide' puts A and ST between the P and the URE of PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasture is land covered with grass for grazing animals.

clue.text: Fighting outside University? Lots here

indicators.note: the fighting word goes round the university letter

parts.note: action is combat, as in killed in action

explanation.surface: Students brawl off campus, many of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' are items for sale under the hammer, not many people.
explanation.definitionFit: A saleroom is where items are sold by bidding, each one numbered as a lot.

clue.text: He could certainly draw game

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A man is sure to end a match level.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiepolo was an 18th-century Venetian painter and draughtsman, so he could certainly draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was a great Venetian artist famous for his frescoes and drawings.

clue.text: Exceeds the resources of such as Lazarus

explanation.surface: Costs too much for the poor, such as the man in the parable.
explanation.walkthrough: To beggar belief or description is to go beyond it; Lazarus is the poor man at the rich man's gate in Luke's parable.
explanation.definitionFit: To beggar something is to outstrip its means, and Lazarus is the archetypal mendicant of the Gospel parable.

clue.text: Throw up quietly? That's difficult to manage

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written from the bottom, reading backwards

parts.note: to lob is to toss or throw high
sh is the call for quiet
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Being sick discreetly is hard to pull off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' looks like vomiting; 'up' reverses LOB to BOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie is British slang for awkward, rebellious and uncooperative.

clue.text: A vet got tipsy at this dance

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal doctor got drunk at this ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' rearranges A VET GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is an old French dance in moderate four-four time.

clue.text: Is up before morning to see wild cat

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, morning

indicators.note: wild means the letters run free and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gets up early to spot a wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IS into SI; 'wild' rearranges SEE into ESE. 'wild' looks like it qualifies the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a breed of domestic feline from Thailand.

clue.text: Native of this country proclaims threat to King

definitions.text: Native of this country proclaims threat to King

parts.words: Native of this country proclaims threat to King
parts.note: a native of the country is a Czech, which said aloud is the chess call announcing an attack on the king

explanation.surface: A patriot announces a plot against the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is the chess piece, and the threat to it is a check, a homophone of the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The former central European state of Czechs and Slovaks, split in 1993.

clue.text: See about girl returning to the pleasure-beach

indicators.note: about means the see word is wrapped round the reversed girl

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: returning means the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, a girl's name

explanation.surface: Look around for a girl coming back to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns DI into ID, which goes inside LO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool or bathing beach.

clue.text: Beam, having a right to enthuse about some little girl

parts.note: a chit is a cheeky young girl
to rave about something is to enthuse over it

explanation.surface: Someone is entitled to gush over a young girl and smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' looks like a smile; it is a timber in a building. A chit is an old word for a slip of a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: An architrave is the main beam resting across the tops of columns in classical building.

clue.text: Beyond description, like votes before the counting

explanation.surface: An election night that was simply indescribable.
explanation.definitionFit: Untold means too great to express, and votes not yet tallied have literally not been counted.

clue.text: A rousing call for retired servicemen

definitions.text: A rousing call for retired servicemen

parts.words: A rousing call for retired servicemen
parts.note: retired here means gone to bed, so the call is the bugle that wakes sleeping soldiers

explanation.surface: A stirring appeal is made for veterans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests pensioners, but it means asleep; 'rousing' means waking up rather than stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call that wakes soldiers in the morning.
